title: Consolidate keyed palette lookup and geometry utility mechanics
description:
## User Mandate

> "Sythesize these into durable tasks. Ensure nothing is lost. We're trying to emphasize consolidation, deduping, decomposition of god classes, and other codebase health improvements"

STRICT. Binding constraints:
- Preserve every accepted mechanism from the 2026-09-02 and 2026-09-03 audits in a durable owner or explicit rejected/unresolved record.
- Consolidate only mechanically identical operations and keep domain semantics in their owning types.
- Do not introduce generic service frameworks, adapter base classes, or speculative abstractions.

## Summary

Extract verified shared mechanics from the mesh and material palette implementations and from duplicated geometry/symmetry transform code, while keeping asset-specific policy in the concrete palette and generator owners.

## Scope

- Share ordinal keyed lookup, usable-key enumeration, and duplicate-key detection between CreatureMeshPalette and CreatureMaterialPalette without changing public asset-typed APIs.
- Inventory and consolidate one tested geometry-transform operation for determinant, winding, normals, bounds, and submesh preservation where semantics match.
- Centralize mirror/reflection mathematics and make the symmetry plane an explicit domain decision. Keep mirroring policy at SDF, skeleton, mesh, and editor callers.
- Review remaining mechanically identical ID policy, tolerance, grid-spec, and finite-check candidates. Do not reopen the validated NumericValidity slice without new evidence.
- Keep material-only default/display-name behavior separate from mesh lookup behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Mesh and material palettes pass the same lookup and duplicate-key behavior tests through one shared implementation.
- Existing ordinal comparison, blank-key rejection, stable ordering, and null-entry behavior remain unchanged.
- Geometry and mirror utility tests cover positive and negative determinant transforms, mirrored winding, normals, submeshes, and X-plane parity.
- No domain-specific hierarchy, shape, appearance, or PartType semantics move into Common without a separate decision.
- Runtime/editor builds and focused palette, geometry, mirror, serialization, and determinism tests pass.

## Validation

Run `dotnet build` for runtime, editor, and focused test projects, then run the matching Unity EditMode/PlayMode tests. Record the call-site inventory and parity evidence before removing any duplicate implementation.

## Findings

Source S04 identifies near-byte-for-byte duplication in CreatureMeshPalette and CreatureMaterialPalette for TryResolve, GetUsableKeys, and HasDuplicateKeys. Sources S05 and S06 identify duplicated mirror/reflection math, mesh transform/winding policy, grid derivation, and raw ID policy as additional candidates. The completed CC-090/TSK-0094 finite-check scope remains closed. This task is the owner for the newly verified palette family and explicitly scoped geometry utility follow-up.

## Blockers

The shared helper must be concrete and dependency-neutral. Preserve Unity serialization constraints and distinguish shared mechanics from material-specific behavior.

## Next Step

Capture the exact palette call-site and behavior inventory, then implement the palette helper with parity tests as the first slice.
